title: Why You Always Win Arguments in Your Own Head
hook: Your brain secretly edits past arguments, always making you the victor.

narration.text: Your brain secretly edits past arguments, always making you the victor.
This happens because of a cognitive bias called egocentric memory.
We unconsciously reconstruct memories, highlighting details that support our own perspective.
Our self-esteem benefits from recalling ourselves as more rational and persuasive.
The details that contradict our views often just fade away or get reinterpreted.
It means we rarely learn from past disagreements as effectively as we could.
Noticing this bias helps us understand others' perspectives more fairly.
Have you ever caught yourself doing this after a disagreement?

description: Ever wonder why you always 'win' arguments when replaying them in your head? It is not just you. This video explains the fascinating cognitive bias behind why we consistently misremember past arguments in our own favour.
topic: why we misremember arguments in our own favour
